text:
alex: kicked off a targeted bench comparing pure-SXM, pure-PCIe, and a mixed-hybrid node (2x A100-SXM + 2x A100-PCIe) across eu-west and us-central. focus: p95 latency and inter-GPU memcpy effects while using kv-cache across devices.

maria: nice. which model/config? :mag:  need seq len + batch sizes.

alex: llama-2-13b, q4f32, seq=2048, bs=1 and bs=4, continuous batching ON, kv-cache enabled. compared fused-attn-v2 vs fallback attn.

jonathan: mixed nodes are noisy. how did you map CUDA devices / NUMA?

alex: experimented with two mappings:
- "SXM-primary": process pinned to socket with NVLink-connected SXMs; CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 then fallback 2,3. cpuset bound cores to the same socket.
- "PCIe-primary": reversed mapping and cpuset.

perf-bot: benchmark-run finished 2026-03-20T14:12:05Z (3 reps per config, 95% CI).

alex: raw p95 latencies (ms) eu-west:
SXM-only: 68
PCIe-only: 112
Hybrid (SXM-primary): 74
Hybrid (PCIe-primary): 130

alex: throughput (tokens/s) bs=4:
SXM-only: 1800
PCIe-only: 950
Hybrid (SXM-primary): 1700
Hybrid (PCIe-primary): 760

maria: big p95 penalty when PCIe primary. traces show memcpy spikes?

alex: yep. snippets from device traces: 
```
[trace] copy_d2d via nvlink gpu0->gpu1: 0.06ms
[trace] cudaMemcpyPeer async gpu1->gpu2 (PCIe): 1.3ms
[trace] kernel queue wait: 0.9ms
[trace] d2d pci-e hop: 1.6ms
```
When KV-cache pages were on a PCIe GPU and primary work on SXM, tail latency spikes correlated with peer copies.

priya: did you try cudaMemcpyAsync prefetch threads to overlap DMA?

alex: yes. async prefetch improved hybrid (PCIe-primary) throughput ~10% and lowered p95 by ~8-12ms in the worst cases, but raised CPU utilization and jitter on host scheduling.

kevin: what about kernel selection? any GPU-specific fallbacks?

alex: fused-attn v2 ran on SXM GPUs. on PCIe GPUs we saw heuristics pick a fallback attn kernel due to occupancy/SM differences. forcing fallback on SXM dropped SXM throughput ~12% (not acceptable).

jonathan: operational takeaway?

alex: for low-latency small-batch traffic route to SXM pools (same NVLink fabric). keep PCIe fleets for high-batch background jobs. when using mixed capacity, ensure routing policy prefers same-fabric GPUs or pre-warm KV on target GPU to avoid cross-fabric peer copies.

maria: can you paste the routing policy snippet you used so we can add to docs?

alex: pseudo-rule we tried: 
```
route if region==eu-west and latency_slo <= 80ms -> prefer pool:sxm-eu
else -> pool:gpu-pcie-eu (burst)
```
That reduced hybrid p95 for production-like traffic.

perf-bot: env & libs: CUDA 12.2, driver 535, cuDNN 8.10. reproducibility depends on driver/kernel.

priya: note on quality: q4f32 had tiny MRR regression (+0.7% drop) when we changed prefetch/mmap behaviour across devices. looks like async copy ordering introduces nondeterministic fp ordering when comparing logprobs. will run differential evals.

alex: follow-up plan: publish recipe in eng-ml/bench-recipes (commands, env, cpuset configs), add an evaluation comparing q4f32 output stability across pure-SXM vs mixed. leaving artifact for whoever owns onboarding templates.

jonathan: TL;DR: SXM wins latency and p95; hybrid ok if NVLink locality preserved; PCIe-primary causes memcpy stalls and big tail. async prefetch helps but costs CPU. recommend autoscaler routing prefer same-fabric pools for latency-sensitive routes. :rocket:
